'''Arthur M. Poskanzer''' (28 June 1931 in New York City – 30 June 2021 in [[Berkeley, California]]<ref name=lbnlobit>[https://www-nsd.lbl.gov/2021/07/06/in-memoriam-art-poskanzer/ Obituary - Art Poskanzer, LBNL Nuclear Science Division]</ref><ref name=PT>{{cite journal|doi=10.1063/PT.3.4947| title=Arthur Poskanzer | year=2022 | last1=Jacobs | first1=Peter M. | journal=Physics Today | volume=75 | issue=2 | page=60 | bibcode=2022PhT....75b..60J | s2cid=246519910 }}</ref>) was an experimental physicist, known for his pioneering work on relativistic nuclear collisions.<ref name=BonnerPrize>[http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?=first_nm=Arthur&last_nm=Poskanzer&year=2008 Arthur M. Poskanzer, 2008 Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physicis Recipient, aps.org]</ref>

Poskanzer received in 1953 his bachelor's degree in physics and chemistry from [[Harvard University]] and in 1954 his master's degree in chemistry from [[Columbia University]]. In 1957 he received his Ph.D. from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in physical chemistry. At Harvard his undergraduate advisor was [[George Kistiakowsky]],<ref name=ORAL>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/45457 |title=Oral History Interviews, Arthur Poskanzer, American Institute of Physics|date=24 September 2021 }}</ref> and at MIT his doctoral advisor was [[Charles D. Coryell|Charles Coryell]].<ref name=PT/>

From 1957 to 1966 Poskanzer was a chemist at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]. From 1966 he worked as a scientist at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] (LBL) and remained on the staff there until 2001, when he retired with emeritus status.<ref name=ACAPref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?poskanzera |title=Arthur W. Poskanzer {{!}} Array of Contemporary Physicists, aip.org |access-date=2016-04-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160508192750/https://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?poskanzera |archive-date=2016-05-08 |url-status=dead}}</ref> From 1978 to 1979 he was the scientific director of [[Bevatron#BEVALAC|Bevalac]]. From 1980 to 1990 he was the leader of the Plastic Ball Experimental Group,<ref name=ACAPref/> which was part of a collaboration between LBL and [[GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research]] (GSI). From 1990 to 1995 he was the head of the Relativistic Collisions Program at LBL.

He is famous as one of the co-discoverers of what nuclear physicists call collective flow; this phenomenon consists of fluidic motion exhibited by nuclear matter, such as quarks and gluons, when compressed to a physical state of high temperature and high energy-density.<ref name=BonnerPrize/> This discovery was made during the collaboration between LBL and GSI.

{{blockquote|Among the many highlights of Poskanzer's career at Berkeley Lab, in addition to his co-discovery of collective flow of nuclear matter, he was the first scientific director of the Bevalac accelerator, the co-founder of the STAR collaboration at the [[Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider]] (RHIC), and one of the leading organizers behind SPS heavy ion program at CERN. He was also a co-discoverer of elliptic flow at RHIC, which has proved to be major experimental evidence for the existence of the quark-gluon plasma, an ephemeral state of matter believed to have existed in the first few microseconds after the universe was born. The elliptic flow paper he co-authored was the first from the STAR collaboration and is now a "famous paper" with over 300 citations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.lbl.gov/today/2007/Oct/04-Thu/bonner-jump.html|title=Berkeley's Arthur Poskander Wins APS Bonner Prize|website=Today at Berkeley Lab, lbl.gov|date=4 October 2007}}</ref>}}

For the academic year 1970/71 he was a Guggenheim Fellow<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/arthur-m-poskanzer/ John Simon Guggenheim Foundation | Arthur M. Poskanzer]</ref> at the [[University of Paris-Sud]] in [[Orsay]]. He was several times a visiting scientist at [[CERN]] (in 1979/80, in 1986/87 and in 1995/96, with the latter two visiting years each supported by Alexander von Humboldt Senior US Scientist Awards).<ref name=ACAPref/>

He married in 1954 and upon his death in 2021 was survived by his widow, their three children, and four grandchildren.<ref name=lbnlobit/>

==Honors and awards==
*1976 — elected a Fellow of the American Physical Society
*1979 — American Chemical Society Award in Nuclear Chemistry<ref>{{cite journal|title=ACS recognizes Poskanzer for nuclear chemistry|journal=Physics Today|date=February 1980|volume=33|issue=2|pages=69–71|doi=10.1063/1.2913947}}</ref>
*1992 — elected a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science
*2008 — [[Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics]]
